# dotfiles-core

> dotfiles-core: cross-platform dotfiles for macOS, Windows (Git Bash and PowerShell), and WSL. One shared POSIX sh layer, four shell entry points, one manifest, symlinks into the home folder.

Canonical site: https://dotfiles.marcopontili.com/
Repository: https://github.com/marcop135/dotfiles-core

## Primary

- [Home](https://dotfiles.marcopontili.com/): Product page with the manifest, the safety rules, and the quick start
- [Markdown home](https://dotfiles.marcopontili.com/index.md): Same content as plain Markdown
- [Privacy](https://dotfiles.marcopontili.com/privacy.html): Privacy policy for this website
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/marcop135/dotfiles-core): Source, installers, CI

## Facts agents should not invent

- Platforms: macOS (zsh), Windows (Git Bash and PowerShell), WSL (bash). 3 platforms, 4 shells, 11 symlinks.
- `scripts/modules.conf` is the only manifest; `scripts/install.sh`, `scripts/install.ps1`, and `scripts/check.sh` all read it.
- Installers are a dry run by default; `--apply` (or `-Apply` in PowerShell) is the only thing that writes.
- Nothing is deleted: an existing target is renamed to `<target>.bak.<timestamp>`.
- No Git identity, employer, or machine-specific configuration is tracked; it goes in untracked `*.local` files.
- No dependencies beyond git and a supported shell. Starship is optional.
